tracks.drift_note: Content offset is 0.000 s at 16 probe points from 18.75 s to 3756 s. The 78 ms once recorded here was the file-DURATION difference (3761.084063 - 3761.005688 = exactly 3 MP3 frames of tail padding), not a misalignment. Compare content offsets, never durations — the spec's 200 ms drift gate fails this convo if implemented on durations, and this convo has zero drift.
tracks.isolation_note: Inter-track correlation ~0; 90 targeted bleed windows peak at r 0.017-0.190 with randomly scattered lag. No de-bleed step needed, and the spec's energy-max rule is a no-op here.
tracks.stray_file: '2020-08-22--t02-00-00pm--thekerp copy.mp3' is a 2024 Audition export of Adam's first 400 s with 55.14 s of his own silence spliced out. Redundant. Do not transcribe it.

cold_open.note: Lifted from 20:41 and MOVED, not copied — its source region was cut from the body, so those words occur exactly once in the transcript and nothing looks duplicated. Consequence: the first turn of the transcript is out of chronological order. A beat or a `since` question anchored at t=0 is quoting a moment twenty minutes in. Everything after 12.084 is in program order.

v0.retain_reason: Cross-ASR diff against v0 is the only working entity-error detector. Scribe's logprob is degenerate (median -3.6e-07) and flags none of the five entity problems; a difflib alignment against v0 surfaced all of them in one pass with no audio.

defects.duplicated_block: segments.v0.jsonl indices 850-1035 (0-based, 186 segments, 1809 words) replay 2750.00-3350.02 s a second time. A chunking bug, not a Whisper loop. Any reader must drop that range. transcript.v0.md is exactly segments-minus-this-block.
defects.content_gap: The entire Heartbleed passage (1623-1642 s) is missing — the strongest verify+since claim in the episode. v0 is a valid diff reference and an invalid fallback input.

v1.asr: ElevenLabs Scribe, word-level timings, diarization on
v1.speaker_confidence_method: Per-track audio ownership. speaker_0 windows are hot on brian.mp3 and speaker_1 windows on thekerp.mp3 by 38.19 dB median across 170 turns / 2302 s of mapped speech, 169/170 turns consistent (99.9% duration-weighted), with the silent track at its noise floor rather than merely quieter. Measured through the audio-verified edit map above; perturbing that map by +/-5 s collapses consistency to 73-79% and any single global offset gives 46-62%, so the separation exists only at the correct alignment. Independently, a second pass searched the offset from scratch in 19 blocks across the hour selecting by maximum absolute correlation, and got 19/19 positive with 0 reversals.
v1.speaker_confidence_caveat: Nothing in the audio proves which human is on which file. The mapping rests on the filename token 'thekerp' plus this file. If the recording service wrote the per-guest files under swapped handles, the conclusion inverts and no test run here can see it.
v1.overlap_note: Both speakers are live for 194.4 s (5.2% of the hour). Do not claim per-turn correctness there. Energy-max disagrees with diarization on 14 of 309 sampled turns, 11% for turns under 1 s — crosstalk, not mislabeling.
v1.cross_check: The archive's speakers.md agrees on all 451 turns, but it is byte-reproducible from scribe-raw.json and therefore corroborates nothing.

known_defects.zero_duration_words: 293 of 11770 words (2.49%) have start == end, clustered in overlap regions. Timeline is sound (starts strictly monotonic) but a clip bound on one of these has an unknown onset. Snap in/out to the nearest word with duration > 0 and pad 250 ms.
known_defects.glued_tokens_note: e.g. 'importantIf', 'soThe' — a naive entity extractor promotes these to proper nouns.
